walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 3: Rhythms of the World — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 3: Rhythms of the World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 3: Rhythms of the World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Paul Simon album famously incorporated South African musical styles?
options: Graceland
Hearts and Bones
So Beautiful or So What
Bridge over Troubled Water

mcqs.q: Which texture features simultaneous variations of a single melody?
options: Homophony
Heterophony
Monophony
Polyphony

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
options: V to I.
IV to I (the 'amen' cadence).
It is the very first section.
ii to V.

mcqs.q: What three notes form a major triad in root position?
options: Root, major third, perfect fifth.
Any three notes played together.
Three consecutive scale notes.
It is the very first section.
